notes:
Account: Acme Financial Services — enterprise banking platform. Focus: dedicated capacity evaluation for production inference.

Key requirements / asks:
- Throughput guarantees: want predictable tokens/sec and embedding qps for peak 9-5 traffic pattern. baseline ask: 200 qps embeddings, 150 concurrent chat sessions with p95 <= 120ms.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets; customer wants contractual p95 120ms for chat in-region, fallback to higher-latency model if violated.
- Reserved GPU planning: prefer reserved pool (on-prem for critical workloads + VPC in cloud). asking for sizing guidance: 4-8 x 80GB GPUs initially, ability to burst to +50% for batch jobs.
- SLA negotiations: discussing 99.9% uptime + latency compliance credits. legal wants clear SLA ladder and incident reporting cadence.

Autoscaling & capacity management specifics discussed:
- Scale-up policy: aggressive scale-up on sustained queue length > 20 for > 30s, provision additional nodes in warm pool first. customer wants max scale-up time 90s for chat-critical paths.
- Scale-down policy: conservative cooldown 15m after idle to avoid oscillation; prefer gradual scale-down (one node at a time) and retain minimum warm pool of 2 instances per region.
- Warm pools: agreed to keep warm pool for low-latency routes (chat) sized to handle 30% of expected peak traffic to meet SLOs; warm pool pre-warm KV cache and model weights.
- Queueing behavior: implement priority queueing (latency-critical vs batch) with separate token budgets; backpressure mechanism to reject or reroute to cheaper model when queue > 100.
- Metrics & observability: need per-route p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, queue depth, warm-pool utilization, cold-starts. Redwood Console dashboards requested.

POC / Next steps:
- POC config: Dedicated reserved 4x80GB equiv GPUs in cloud VPC + on-prem fallback for regulated endpoints; warm pool of 2 nodes; autoscale rules as above.
- Workshop scheduled: week of 2026-03-08 to finalize GPU counts, quantization profile, and test traffic scripts.
- Legal/SLA: send draft SLA including latency SLO ladder and credits (owner: Maya).

Quotes & direct notes:
- CTO: "We need rock-solid latency during market hours — any plan that requires >2m to scale up is non-starter."
- Head of Infrastructure: "Warm pools sound promising but we need cost model — how much will idle warm nodes add to ARR?"
- SE note: "Will run load tests with mixed chat+embeddings traffic; need sample traffic trace from Acme."

Short-term blockers:
- IT security needs HSM/KMS integration doc and penetration test results
- CFO wants an in-depth cost estimate comparing warm pool sizes and autoscale delta

Overall: Account is high priority. Strong likelihood to convert to Dedicated if POC meets latency and autoscaling objectives. Keep legal and infra loops tight.
